findings.reason: Massachusetts state law (M.G.L. c. 40P § 4) bars cities and towns from enacting, maintaining or enforcing rent control of any kind. The only exception is for a municipality that accepts the chapter. Even then, compliance is voluntary after six months. It cannot cover owners of fewer than ten rental units or units with fair market rent over $400. The municipality must also pay owners the difference from market rent out of general funds. No mandatory rent control is in effect under this section.

findings.reason: New Jersey has no statewide rent control or rent cap law; rent control exists only through municipal ordinances. Qualified: related enacted rules exist at this level: NJ-RENT-01 (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(f)): No numeric cap; increase must not be unconscionable; NJ-RENT-02 (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5): 30 years after completion of construction.
findings.quoted_span: The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents.
